literature.headline_zh: 人偏肺病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人偏肺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在两个Nirsevimab使用季节后,RSV病例的下降趋势持续,而hMPV仍然是严重支气管炎的重要原因。具体而言,hMPV在住院儿童中被检测到的比例为15%,其发病率与RSV相比没有显著减少。 [10.1097/inf.0000000000005447]
识别出三个系统发育上不同的簇,其中簇3显示出最高的进化速率、最大的系统发育多样性和最显著的近期种群动态变化。所有簇的整体蛋白相似性均超过97%,且299个密码子(约55%)始终处于负选择下。 [10.3390/microorganisms14102386]
综述发现,hMPV(1.4%)的所有原因发病率并不高于流感(2.2–33.3%)或RSV(0–25%)。所有病毒之间的ICU入院率高度变异且重叠。一项单一研究报告了hMPV的中位住院时间(9天)明显长于RSV(18天)和流感(10–13天)。 [10.1186/s12879-026-14629-0]
在590名hMPV阳性患者中,有192名成人被纳入研究;其中121名作为门诊患者管理,71名住院治疗。在68名成人中发现了肺炎,包括71名住院患者中的43名。到2025年,门诊患者中有24.0%被发现患有肺炎,住院患者中有65.5%被发现患有肺炎。 [10.3390/jcm15208025]
多重PCR检测到至少一种呼吸道病原体的患者占69.2%,其中人呼吸道合胞病毒(HRSV)A/B是最常见的病原体。未检测到人偏肺病毒病例,其他病原体如沙眼衣原体肺炎、肠道病毒和肺炎支原体也未被发现。 [PMCID:PMC13664063]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: After two seasons of Nirsevimab use, the decline in RSV cases continued, while hMPV remained a significant cause of severe bronchiolitis. Specifically, hMPV was detected in 15% of hospitalized children, with no substantial reduction in its incidence compared to RSV. [10.1097/inf.0000000000005447]

Three phylogenetically distinct clusters were identified, with Cluster 3 showing the highest evolutionary rate, greatest phylogenetic diversity, and the most recent demographic fluctuations. [10.3390/microorganisms14102386]

The review found that all-cause mortality for HMPV (1.4%) was not higher than for influenza (2.2–33.3%) or RSV (0–25%). ICU admission rates were highly variable and overlapping across all viruses. [10.1186/s12879-026-14629-0]

Among 590 hMPV-positive patients, 192 adults were included; 121 were managed as outpatients and 71 were hospitalized. Pneumonia was identified in 68 adults, including 43 of 71 hospitalized patients. By 2025, pneumonia was identified in 24.0% of outpatients and 65.5% of hospitalized patients. [10.3390/jcm15208025]
Multiplex PCR detected at least one respiratory pathogen in 69.2% of patients, with human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) A/B being the most frequently identified. [PMCID:PMC13664063]

literature.en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments. After two seasons of Nirsevimab use, the decline in RSV cases continued, while hMPV remained a significant cause of severe bronchiolitis. Three phylogenetically distinct clusters were identified, with Cluster 3 showing the highest evolutionary rate, greatest phylogenetic diversity, and the most recent demographic fluctuations. The review found that all-cause mortality for HMPV (1.4%) was not higher than for influenza (2.2–33.3%) or RSV (0–25%). ICU admission rates were highly variable and overlapping across all viruses. Among 590 hMPV-positive patients, 192 adults were included; 121 were managed as outpatients and 71 were hospitalized. Pneumonia was identified in 68 adults, including 43 of 71 hospitalized patients.

news.headline_zh: 人偏肺病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期人偏肺病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 来自河南省的一项大型哨点 人偏肺病毒 研究显示,人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 在 2024 年底在中国中部地区急剧复苏,随后在 2025 年显着下降。Bioengineer.org 报道了该研究。 [news-eda5eb4b76c9aead]
一项血清流行病学研究显示,16 至 36 个月大的幼儿对 人偏肺病毒 的免疫防御能力最弱,只有 67.8% 的血清反应呈阳性,几何平均滴度为 217。Bioengineer.org 于 2026 年 10 月 19 日报道了这一发现。 [news-e3a16f452ab98f71]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Human metapneumovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: A large sentinel surveillance study from Henan Province revealed a dramatic resurgence of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) in central China in late 2024, followed by a significant decline in 2025. The study was reported by Bioengineer.org. [news-eda5eb4b76c9aead]

A seroepidemiological study revealed that toddlers aged 16 to 36 months showed the weakest immune defenses against human metapneumovirus, with only 67.8% seropositive and a geometric mean titer of 217. This finding was reported by Bioengineer.org on October 19, 2026. [news-e3a16f452ab98f71]

A large sentinel surveillance study from Henan Province revealed a dramatic resurgence of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) in central China in late 2024, followed by a significant decline in 2025. papers.title: Molecular Evolution of the HMPV-A Fusion Gene Reveals Lineage-Specific Diversification and Structural Conservation
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus genotype A (HMPV-A) comprises genetically diverse lineages, but whether F-gene diversification is accompanied by changes in the conserved fusion (F) protein remains unclear. We analyzed 500 PARNAS-selected HMPV-A F gene sequences from 25 countries collected between 1982 and 2025 using time-scaled phylogenetics, Bayesian skyline analysis, evolutionary-rate and patristic-distance estimation, codon-based selection analysis, sequence-identity profiling, and structural epitope modeling. Three phylogenetically distinct clusters were identified. Cluster 1 diverged from the common ancestor of Clusters 2 and 3 around 1927. Cluster 3 comprised 435 representative sequences and showed the highest estimated evolutionary rate, greatest phylogenetic diversity, and the most pronounced recent demographic fluctuations. The overall evolutionary rate was 9.20 × 10−4 substitutions/site/year. Despite nucleotide-level diversification, whole-protein identity exceeded 97% in all clusters, 299 codons (approximately 55%) were consistently under negative selection, whereas positive-selection signals were limited and method-specific, with MEME identifying codons 188 and 271 and FUBAR identifying codon 528. Major neutralizing antibody-binding regions were largely conserved, and the six modeled representatives showed similar global F-protein backbone structures and predicted epitope-surface distributions, although A61S and K143T occurred within neutralizing antibody-binding sites and require experimental evaluation. These findings demonstrate lineage-specific F gene diversification under strong functional constraint and support the HMPV F protein as a broadly conserved intervention target.

The study highlights the F protein's potential as a broadly conserved target for interventions, though limitations include the lack of experimental validation for epitopes. papers.title: Outcomes of ‘neglected’ respiratory viruses (PIV, hMPV) vs. Influenza and RSV lower respiratory tract infections in hematologic malignancies: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory viral lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) are a major cause of mortality and morbidity in adults with hematological malignancies. While influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are well-characterized, the comparative clinical burden of parainfluenza virus (PIV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) remains poorly defined. Methods We conducted a systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD420251152933) following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We searched four databases from inception to October 2025 for observational studies comparing clinical outcomes of PIV/hMPV LRTI versus RSV/influenza pneumonia in adults undergoing chemotherapy for hematological malignancies. Primary outcomes were all-cause mortality, ICU admission, mechanical ventilation, and length of stay. Dual independent review was performed for study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale). A narrative synthesis was conducted. Results From 1,071 screened records, 12 studies (11 ‘Good’ quality) comprising a total of 4,841 patients were included. Data for mechanical ventilation were particularly scarce, and notably absent for PIV and Influenza. All-cause mortality for PIV (0–16%) and hMPV (1.4%) was not higher than for influenza (2.2–33.3%) or RSV (0–25%). ICU admission rates were highly variable and overlapping across all viruses. A salient finding, derived from a single study, was a substantially prolonged median length of hospital stay for PIV (28 days) compared to RSV (18 days), hMPV (9 days), and influenza (10–13 days). Conclusion PIV and hMPV LRTI present a distinct clinical profile in this vulnerable population. While mortality is comparable to more common viruses, PIV infection was reported in a single, small-cohort study to be associated with a prolonged hospital stay, suggesting a potential morbidity burden that requires further validation. These findings challenge the perception of these pathogens as uniformly less severe and highlight an urgent need for prospective studies to guide optimized management and resource allocation.

analysis.scope_and_question: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection and disease in adults with hematological malignancies. analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, with dual independent review for study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Four databases were searched from inception to October 2025 for observational studies comparing clinical outcomes of HMPV LRTI with those of RSV and influenza pneumonia in adults undergoing chemotherapy for hematological malignancies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review found that all-cause mortality for HMPV (1.4%) was not higher than for influenza (2.2–33.3%) or RSV (0–25%). ICU admission rates were highly variable and overlapping across all viruses. A single study reported a substantially prolonged median length of hospital stay for HMPV (9 days) compared to RSV (18 days) and influenza (10–13 days).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Data for mechanical ventilation were particularly scarce, and notably absent for HMPV and influenza. The findings suggest that HMPV infection may have a distinct clinical profile, but the evidence is limited and requires further validation. The review highlights the need for prospective studies to better understand the morbidity burden of HMPV in this population.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prospective studies are urgently needed to guide optimized management and resource allocation for HMPV LRTI in adults with hematological malignancies. The review emphasizes the importance of further research to clarify the clinical significance of HMPV infections and to improve surveillance and diagnostic strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the clinical outcomes of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) in adults with hematological malignancies, comparing them to those of influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The review found that all-cause mortality for HMPV was not higher than for influenza or RSV, but a single study reported a significantly prolonged median length of hospital stay for HMPV compared to RSV and influenza. ICU admission rates were highly variable across all viruses, and data on mechanical ventilation were limited. The findings suggest that HMPV may have a distinct clinical profile in this vulnerable population, highlighting the need for further prospective studies to better understand its morbidity burden and guide management strategies.

papers.title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
papers.abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

The evidence highlights the virus's targeting of respiratory epithelium and the immune responses it triggers. While investigational therapies like fusion and protease inhibitors show promise, their efficacy remains unproven. Vaccine development is ongoing, with several candidates in early stages. papers.abstract_zh: 引言:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可在不同年龄段人群中引发感染,尤其是在幼儿、免疫功能低下者及老年人中。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或针对人偏肺病毒的特异性治疗方法,亟需进一步研究治疗和预防策略。方法:通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。结果:研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,触发免疫应答,这些免疫应答既有助于病毒清除,也会导致疾病发病机制。正在研发的治疗方法,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但仍需进一步验证。免疫调节剂和中草药可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的有效性尚未得到证实。疫苗研发取得进展,多个候选疫苗已进入临床前及早期临床阶段。讨论:由于人偏肺病毒的季节性流行、与其他呼吸道病毒的临床相似性以及缺乏特异性治疗方法,该病毒继续对公共卫生构成重大负担。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度增加,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管目前主要采用支持性治疗,但新兴的抗病毒药物和疫苗可能为未来提供解决方案。改善诊断可及性、提高公众意识及开展针对性研究对于控制人偏肺病毒感染至关重要。结论:由于缺乏针对性治疗方法和疫苗,人偏肺病毒继续对公共卫生构成挑战。针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。亟需进一步临床试验以确立安全有效的治疗方案。

papers.title: Clinical Factors Associated with Documented Radiographic Pneumonia in Adults with Human Metapneumovirus Infection: A Hospital-Wide Cohort Study in Japan
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is increasingly recognized as an important cause of adult respiratory infection, but data on pneumonia remain limited. We evaluated clinical characteristics, temporal detection patterns, and clinical factors associated with radiographic pneumonia among adults with laboratory-confirmed hMPV infection. Methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study at Kyorin University Hospital, Tokyo, Japan, from December 2020 to February 2026. Adults aged ≥18 years with hMPV detected by multiplex polymerase chain reaction were included. The primary outcome, documented radiographic pneumonia, was defined by newly identified pneumonia-compatible parenchymal abnormalities on chest radiography and/or chest computed tomography (CT). Logistic regression was used to identify clinical factors associated with this outcome. Results: Among 590 hMPV-positive patients, 192 adults were included; 121 were managed as outpatients and 71 were hospitalized. Pneumonia was identified in 68 adults, including 43 of 71 hospitalized patients. Adult hMPV detection shifted from summer predominance in 2022–2023 toward increased spring and winter detections in 2024–2025 after the onset of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. By 2025, pneumonia was identified in 24.0% of outpatients and 65.5% of hospitalized patients. In the primary multivariable model, higher C-reactive protein (CRP) concentrations (adjusted odds ratio per 1 mg/dL, 1.12; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.03–1.22; p = 0.008) and abnormal auscultation (adjusted odds ratio, 3.45; 95% CI, 1.21–9.83; p = 0.021) were independently associated with pneumonia. Conclusions: Adult hMPV infection was frequently associated with radiographic pneumonia, particularly among hospitalized patients. Elevated C-reactive protein concentrations and abnormal auscultation may help identify adults with hMPV infection who are more likely to have pneumonia.

papers.title_zh: 与成人人偏肺病毒感染患者影像学肺炎相关临床因素:日本东京Kyorin大学医院全院范围队列研究研究
papers.source_body_en: Background/Objectives: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is increasingly recognized as an important cause of adult respiratory infection, but data on pneumonia remain limited. We evaluated clinical characteristics, temporal detection patterns, and clinical factors associated with radiographic pneumonia among adults with laboratory-confirmed hMPV infection. Methods: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study at Kyorin University Hospital, Tokyo, Japan, from December 2020 to February 2026. Adults aged ≥18 years with hMPV detected by multiplex polymerase chain reaction were included. The primary outcome, documented radiographic pneumonia, was defined by newly identified pneumonia-compatible parenchymal abnormalities on chest radiography and/or chest computed tomography (CT). Logistic regression was used to identify clinical factors associated with this outcome. Results: Among 590 hMPV-positive patients, 192 adults were included; 121 were managed as outpatients and 71 were hospitalized. Pneumonia was identified in 68 adults, including 43 of 71 hospitalized patients. Adult hMPV detection shifted from summer predominance in 2022–2023 toward increased spring and winter detections in 2024–2025 after the onset of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. By 2025, pneumonia was identified in 24.0% of outpatients and 65.5% of hospitalized patients. In the primary multivariable model, higher C-reactive protein (CRP) concentrations (adjusted odds ratio per 1 mg/dL, 1.12; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.03–1.22; p = 0.008) and abnormal auscultation (adjusted odds ratio, 3.45; 95% CI, 1.21–9.83; p = 0.021) were independently associated with pneumonia. Conclusions: Adult hMPV infection was frequently associated with radiographic pneumonia, particularly among hospitalized patients. Elevated C-reactive protein concentrations and abnormal auscultation may help identify adults with hMPV infection who are more likely to have pneumonia.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景/目的:人偏肺病毒(hMPV)正逐渐被认识到是成人呼吸道感染的重要原因,但关于肺炎的数据仍然有限。我们评估了实验室确诊hMPV感染的成人患者中与放射学肺炎相关的临床特征、时间检测模式及临床因素。方法:我们在日本东京的Kyorin大学医院进行了一项单中心回顾性观察研究,时间从2020年12月至2026年2月。纳入标准为年龄≥18岁且通过多重聚合酶链反应检测出hMPV的成人。主要结局是记录的放射学肺炎,定义为胸部X光和/或胸部计算机断层扫描(CT)上新发现的符合肺炎特征的实质病变。使用逻辑回归分析确定与该结局相关的临床因素。结果:在590名hMPV阳性患者中,有192名成人被纳入研究;其中121名作为门诊患者管理,71名住院治疗。在68名成人中发现了肺炎,包括71名住院患者中的43名。自冠状病毒疾病2019(COVID-19)大流行开始后,成人hMPV检测的季节分布从2022–2023年的夏季为主转变为2024–2025年的春季和冬季增加。到2025年,门诊患者中有24.0%被发现患有肺炎,住院患者中有65.5%被发现患有肺炎。在主要的多变量模型中,较高的C反应蛋白(CRP)浓度(每1 mg/dL调整比值比为1.12;95%置信区间(CI)为1.03–1.22;p = 0.008)和异常听诊(调整比值比为3.45;95% CI为1.21–9.83;p = 0.021)与肺炎独立相关。结论:成人hMPV感染常与放射学肺炎相关,尤其是在住院患者中。升高的C反应蛋白浓度和异常听诊可能有助于识别更可能患有肺炎的hMPV感染成人。

papers.full_text: AbstractBackground: Severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) remain a major cause of hospitalization and mortality, particularly among children and other vulnerable populations. Early identification of pathogens and disease severity is essential for clinical decision-making. This study evaluated the etiology of non-SARS-CoV-2 SARI and the prognostic utility of the ViVI Disease Severity Score (ViVI Score) in a predominantly pediatric cohort.Methods: In this retrospective study, 117 hospitalized SARS-CoV-2-negative SARI patients, including 103 children and 14 adults, admitted to a tertiary care hospital in North India between September and December 2021 were evaluated. Respiratory pathogens were identified using multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR), alongside blood and lower respiratory tract cultures. Serum C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and D-dimer were measured. Mortality prediction was assessed using the ViVI Score and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.Results: The median age was 2.0 years (interquartile range, 0.5-7.5 years). Multiplex PCR detected respiratory pathogens in 69.2% of patients, with human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) A/B predominating. Blood cultures were positive in 40/117 patients (34.2%), predominantly yielding methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Overall mortality was 20.5%, increasing to 60% among patients with culture-confirmed sepsis. Elevated CRP and PCT were observed in all septic patients. The ViVI Score showed excellent mortality prediction (area under the curve (AUC) 0.946). A cutoff of ≥30 yielded 83.3% sensitivity and 91.4% specificity and was strongly associated with mortality (OR 53.1, 95% CI 14.5-194.0; p<0.001).Conclusion: HRSV was the predominant respiratory pathogen, whereas bacterial sepsis was the principal determinant of mortality. Multiplex molecular diagnostics combined with standardized severity assessment may improve clinical triage, antimicrobial stewardship, and respiratory pathogen surveillance in resource-limited settings.Keywords: mortality, multiplex pcr, respiratory syncytial virus, sepsis, severe acute respiratory infection, vivi disease severity score Materials and methodsStudy design and settingThis retrospective observational study analyzed laboratory and clinical data of patients admitted with severe acute respiratory syndrome during the defined period from September to December 2021, corresponding to the COVID-19 pandemic, at a tertiary care teaching hospital in North India. The data analysis was undertaken subsequently in the post-pandemic phase. The study was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi, India (Approval Ref No. IEC/VMMC/SJH/Cert./05-2024/54, dated 23/07/2024).The primary objective was to establish an etiological profile of pathogens responsible for SARI other than SARS-CoV-2 among hospitalized patients, using a combination of multiplex PCR and conventional microbiological culture. Clinical and laboratory data were retrieved retrospectively from hospital records. The study population was predominantly pediatric, comprising 103 children and 14 adults.Sampling technique and patient selectionConsecutive patients admitted during the study period with signs and symptoms of acute respiratory illness were screened for inclusion. Patients meeting the WHO SARI case definition, with fever ≥38°C and cough, with symptom onset within the last 10 days, requiring hospitalization, were included in the study [1]. The study cohort comprised predominantly pediatric patients, with 103 children and 14 adults.Pathogen detection and laboratory methodsRT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal swabs were collected from all SARI patients in the hospital during that period and tested for SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR. Patients who tested negative for SARS-CoV-2 were included in this study and were subjected to multiplex PCR. Testing was performed in a designated COVID-19 molecular diagnostic laboratory, following Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) guidelines [8] and using ICMR-National Institute of Virology-approved commercial RT-PCR kits. The test targeted specific viral genes (e.g., E, ORF) for detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA.Multiplex PCR for Respiratory PathogensRespiratory specimens (nasopharyngeal/throat swabs) were further subjected to multiplex PCR using the Fast-Track Diagnostics Respiratory Pathogens 21 Plus (Fast-Track Diagnostics, Junglinster, Luxembourg). This assay detects Chlamydia pneumoniae, Enterovirus, Haemophilus influenzae B, Human adenovirus, Human bocavirus, Human coronavirus 229E, Human coronavirus HKU1, Human coronavirus NL63, Human coronavirus OC43, Human metapneumoviruses A/B, Human parainfluenza virus 1-4, Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) A/B, Human rhinovirus, Influenza A virus, Influenza A (H1N1) virus, Influenza B virus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae. Tests were conducted according to the manufacturer's protocol, including appropriate internal and external controls.Conventional Microbiological CultureBlood cultures were performed in all 117 enrolled patients using the BacT/ALERT® automated system (bioMérieux, France). Samples that flagged positive were subcultured on blood and MacConkey agar plates, followed by identification using standard microbiological techniques [9,10]. Patients with positive blood cultures were clinically evaluated and classified as having sepsis based on the treating clinical team's assessment and documented clinical findings. All 40 patients with positive blood cultures were clinically diagnosed with sepsis. The lower respiratory tract samples were processed using standard microbiological techniques [9,10]. Isolates were identified by morphology, Gram staining, and biochemical profiling.BiomarkersSerum C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and D-dimer were measured on the Mispa i3 automated cartridge-based specific protein analyser (Agappe Diagnostics Ltd., Kerala, India). The platform uses a dual-channel system (rate-based nephelometry and turbidimetry/photometry) and prefilled single-use reagent cartridges with test-specific IC-card (smart card) calibration.Disease severity assessmentThe ViVI Score was used to assess disease severity based on 22 clinical parameters, with a total score ranging from 0 to 48 [11,12]. The scoring was weighted as follows: Disease Severity with Uncomplicated Symptoms (DSU): Weight=1×; Disease Severity with Complicated Symptoms (DSC): Weight=3×; Total Disease Severity Score=DSU + DSC. A schematic representation of the study methodology is shown in Figure 1.Figure 1Schematic representation of the study methodologyFast-Track 21 (Fast-Track Diagnostics, Junglinster, Luxembourg); BacT/ALERT® (bioMérieux, France)PCR: polymerase chain reaction; ET: endotrachealStatistical analysisPathogen distributions and descriptive statistics (median, IQR) were calculated in Microsoft Excel (Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, Washington, United States), and odds ratios were estimated using Fisher’s exact test. Diagnostic performance of the ViVI Score for outcome classification was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis of ordinal rating data in JROCFIT v2.0.1 (John Eng; based on ROCFIT by Metz et al.) [13]: outcomes were coded as positive = survival (alive) and negative = death, ViVI scores were converted into an ordinal rating scale in which higher categories represented stronger evidence of the positive state, and a maximum-likelihood unequal-variance binormal ROC model was fitted to estimate the area under the curve (AUC) with its standard deviation; because ViVI is a severity index (higher scores indicate poorer prognosis), the ratings were oriented such that lower ViVI scores corresponded to stronger evidence of survival. ResultsA total of 117 patients were included in the study. The cohort was predominantly pediatric, comprising 103 children and 14 adults. The median age of the study population was 2.0 years (IQR 0.5-7.5 years). The male-to-female ratio was 1.81:1, indicating a male predominance.Pathogen detection profile from the multiplex PCROut of the 117 patients, 81 (69.2%) were positive for at least one respiratory pathogen using multiplex PCR. Multiplex respiratory pathogen testing identified HRSV A/B as the most frequently detected pathogen (n=60), followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae (n=16), Staphylococcus aureus (n=11), human rhinovirus (n=8), and influenza B virus (n=7). Lower detection rates were observed for human parainfluenza virus type 4 (n=3), human adenovirus (n=2), human coronavirus OC43, human metapneumovirus A/B, human parainfluenza virus type 3, and human parechovirus (each n=1). No cases were detected for Chlamydophila pneumoniae, enterovirus, Haemophilus influenzae, human bocavirus, human coronaviruses 229E, HKU1, and NL63, human parainfluenza virus types 1 and 2, influenza A virus (including H1N1), or Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Conversely, 36 patients tested negative for all pathogens, indicating either non-infectious etiologies or undetected organisms outside the panel’s scope (Figure 2). Additionally, six cases of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) due to HRSV were documented in a subset of adult patients, along with HRSV positivity among 13 children with underlying hematological disorders.Figure 2Distribution of pathogen positivity by multiplex PCR in patient samplesHRSV A/B was the most frequently identified organism, followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Rhinovirus.mPCR+: multiplex polymerase chain reaction positive for at least one pathogen; RSV A/B: respiratory syncytial virus types A and B; S. pneumonia: Streptococcus pneumoniae; S. aureus: Staphylococcus aureus; HRV: human rhinovirus; IBV: influenza B virus; HPIV-4: human parainfluenza virus type 4; HAdV: human adenovirus; HCoV-OC43: human coronavirus OC43; HMPV A/B: human metapneumovirus types A and B; HPIV-3: human parainfluenza virus type 3; HPeV: human parechovirus; NPD: no pathogen detected; ARDS: acute respiratory distress syndrome; HD: hematological disordersPathogen detection profile from conventional culturesBlood cultures were positive in 40/117 patients (34.2%); five were adults, and 35 were children. Among the positive blood cultures, 18 yielded methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus, seven Escherichia coli, seven Klebsiella pneumoniae, seven Streptococcus pneumoniae, and one yielded both S. aureus and S. pneumoniae. Lower respiratory tract aerobic cultures were positive in 48 patients (five adults and 43 children), yielding S. pneumoniae in 15, E. coli in 12, confluent growth of K. pneumoniae in 10, and S. aureus in 10; one patient had both S. pneumoniae and S. aureus.Biomarker profileElevated PCT (>0.5 ng/mL) was observed in 55/117 patients (47.0%), including all 40 patients with positive blood cultures. Markedly elevated CRP (>10 mg/dL) was observed in 101/117 patients (86.3%), including all 40 patients with positive blood cultures. Positive D-dimer, suggestive of a hypercoagulable state, was observed in 35 patients, of whom 30 had sepsis.ViVI Score distributionThe median ViVI Score across all patients was 22. Distribution of ViVI scores varied based on pathogen and infection type. Among single infections, HRSV A/B was most frequent (n=38) with a median ViVI score of 20.5 (IQR 13.5). Other single pathogens were less common, including Staphylococcus aureus (n=5; median 20 (IQR 19)), Influenza B (n=4; median 20.5 (IQR 10.25)), Streptococcus pneumoniae (n=3; median 29 (IQR 6.5)), Human rhinovirus (n=2; median 35 (IQR 6)), and individual cases of adenovirus (median 37) and parainfluenza virus 4 (median 42). Among coinfections, HRSV + Streptococcus pneumoniae was the most common (n=10; median 21 (IQR 13.75)). Other HRSV coinfections included HRSV + rhinovirus (n=3; median 20 (IQR 4)), HRSV + Influenza B (n=2; median 32 (IQR 16)), and HRSV + Staphylococcus aureus (n=2; median 20 (IQR 3)), while the remaining coinfections occurred as single cases with variable ViVI scores (Table 1).Table 1Distribution of median ViVI Scores across respiratory pathogens and coinfectionsThe table summarizes the median ViVI score with the corresponding interquartile range (IQR) for each identified organism or organism combination, along with the number of affected patients and classification as single infection or coinfection. ViVI scores reflect clinical severity at presentation, with higher scores indicating greater disease severity. Coinfections include viral-viral and viral-bacterial combinations detected by multiplex PCR and/or standard microbiological methods.HRSV: human respiratory syncytial virus; PCR: polymerase chain reaction; ViVI Score: ViVI Disease Severity ScoreOrganism / CoinfectionMedian ViVI scoreIQR (interquartile range)Number of patientsType of infectionHuman respiratory syncytial viruses A/B20.513.538Single InfectionStaphylococcus aureus20195Single InfectionInfluenza B virus20.510.254Single InfectionStreptococcus pneumoniae296.53Single InfectionHuman rhinovirus3562Single InfectionHuman adenovirus3701Single InfectionHuman parainfluenza virus 44201Single InfectionHRSV + Streptococcus pneumoniae 2113.7510CoinfectionHRSV + Human rhinovirus2043CoinfectionHRSV + Influenza B virus32162CoinfectionHRSV + Staphylococcus aureus 2032CoinfectionAdenovirus + HRSV1601CoinfectionCoronavirus OC43 + HRSV1601CoinfectionMetapneumovirus + HRSV4501CoinfectionParainfluenza virus 3 + Parainfluenza virus 41101CoinfectionParainfluenza virus 4 + Parechovirus801CoinfectionRhinovirus + Staphylococcus aureus 2901CoinfectionInfluenza B virus + Streptococcus pneumoniae 2901CoinfectionStaphylococcus aureus + Streptococcus pneumoniae 3501CoinfectionHRSV + Parainfluenza virus 41501CoinfectionHRSV + Influenza B + Staphylococcus aureus 2701CoinfectionClinical outcomes and mortalityThe overall mortality rate in the cohort was 20.5% (24/117). Of particular concern was the subgroup of patients presenting with SARI and culture-confirmed sepsis (n=40), in which mortality rose dramatically to 60% (24/40). This suggests that progression to sepsis remains the strongest indicator of poor outcomes in SARI cases.Predictive utility of the ViVI ScoreA total of 117 cases were analyzed (93 survivors and 24 deaths). ROC analysis using JROCFIT demonstrated excellent discrimination between survivors and non-survivors (fitted AUC 0.946 (SD 0.022); empiric AUC 0.942) (Figure 3).Figure 3Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve demonstrating the predictive performance of the ViVI Disease Severity Score for mortalityThe ROC plot displays the relationship between the false positive fraction (FPF: 1 − specificity) on the x-axis and the true positive fraction (TPF: sensitivity) on the y-axis across decision thresholds. The blue curve with red markers represents the binormal ROC curve fitted using maximum-likelihood estimation (JROCFIT), while the grey envelopes depict the 95% confidence interval around the fitted curve. The empirical (nonparametric) ROC operating points are shown as black markers (with the green connection, where applicable). Overall discrimination was excellent (fitted AUC ≈ 0.946; empirical AUC ≈ 0.942), with the curve lying close to the upper-left corner, indicating high sensitivity at low false-positive rates.The ROC curve lies close to the upper-left corner, indicating excellent discriminatory performance of the ViVI Score for predicting mortality across a range of decision thresholds (Figure 3). Using the ViVI Score as a mortality predictor and classifying death as the event, a low cutoff of ViVI ≥15 yielded 100% sensitivity for death (24/24) but low specificity (29.0%, 27/93) (TP=24, FN=0, TN=27, FP=66). In contrast, a high cutoff of ViVI ≥45 yielded 100% specificity (93/93) but low sensitivity (25.0%, 6/24) (TP=6, FN=18, TN=93, FP=0). The optimal threshold by Youden's J was ViVI ≥30, which provided balanced performance (sensitivity 83.3% (20/24) and specificity 91.4% (85/93); overall accuracy 89.7% (105/117)) (TP=20, FN=4, TN=85, FP=8). Patients with ViVI ≥30 had markedly increased odds of death compared with those with ViVI <30 (odds ratio 53.1, 95% CI 14.5-194.0; Fisher's exact test p=1.4 × 10−12). DiscussionThe present study provides a comprehensive etiological and clinical profile of non-SARS-CoV-2 SARI in a predominantly pediatric cohort, with simultaneous assessment of respiratory pathogens, bacterial culture results, inflammatory biomarkers, and disease severity. Multiplex PCR detected at least one respiratory pathogen in 69.2% of patients, while HRSV A/B was the predominant respiratory pathogen. Culture-confirmed bloodstream infection was associated with substantially higher mortality, and the ViVI Score demonstrated excellent discrimination for mortality.The 69.2% pathogen detection rate observed with multiplex PCR is consistent with previous studies demonstrating substantial pathogen detection among patients with severe respiratory infection. El Kholy et al. reported a high rate of viral detection and frequent co-detection in children with SARI, while Contier et al. demonstrated the diagnostic performance of multiplex PCR among critically ill immunocompromised patients [14,15]. Differences in age distribution, disease severity, sampling practices, seasonality, and the respiratory pathogen panels used may account for variations in diagnostic yield between studies.HRSV A/B was the predominant respiratory pathogen in our cohort. This finding is consistent with surveillance studies from different geographical settings, including Senegal, India, and Suriname, which have identified HRSV as an important cause of severe respiratory illness and hospitalization among children [16-18]. full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionThe present study provides a comprehensive etiological and clinical profile of non-SARS-CoV-2 SARI in a predominantly pediatric cohort, with simultaneous assessment of respiratory pathogens, bacterial culture results, inflammatory biomarkers, and disease severity. Multiplex PCR detected at least one respiratory pathogen in 69.2% of patients, while HRSV A/B was the predominant respiratory pathogen. Culture-confirmed bloodstream infection was associated with substantially higher mortality, and the ViVI Score demonstrated excellent discrimination for mortality.The 69.2% pathogen detection rate observed with multiplex PCR is consistent with previous studies demonstrating substantial pathogen detection among patients with severe respiratory infection. El Kholy et al. reported a high rate of viral detection and frequent co-detection in children with SARI, while Contier et al. demonstrated the diagnostic performance of multiplex PCR among critically ill immunocompromised patients [14,15]. Differences in age distribution, disease severity, sampling practices, seasonality, and the respiratory pathogen panels used may account for variations in diagnostic yield between studies.HRSV A/B was the predominant respiratory pathogen in our cohort. This finding is consistent with surveillance studies from different geographical settings, including Senegal, India, and Suriname, which have identified HRSV as an important cause of severe respiratory illness and hospitalization among children [16-18]. The global burden of HRSV is substantial. A systematic analysis estimated 33.0 million HRSV-associated acute lower respiratory infection episodes, 3.6 million hospital admissions, and 101,400 deaths among children younger than five years in 2019, with the majority of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries [19].The frequency of co-infections observed in our cohort is also consistent with previous pediatric SARI studies using multiplex molecular platforms. Lamrani Hanchi et al. reported pathogen detection in 72.5% of hospitalized children and co-infection in 23.3%, highlighting the ability of multiplex PCR to identify multiple respiratory pathogens from a single clinical specimen [20]. Similarly, studies incorporating digital surveillance and virological characterization have emphasized the value of combining pathogen detection with standardized clinical information [21,22]. These findings support the use of syndromic molecular testing as an adjunct to conventional microbiological investigations in patients with severe respiratory disease. However, detection of a respiratory pathogen does not necessarily establish causality, particularly for respiratory viruses that may be detected during prolonged shedding or asymptomatic infection. Therefore, multiplex PCR results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings, disease severity, and conventional microbiological results.The exceptionally high mortality observed among SARI patients with culture-confirmed sepsis (60%) was substantially higher than the overall mortality in the cohort. This finding is consistent with pediatric intensive-care data demonstrating significant mortality among children with bloodstream-infection-associated severe sepsis [23]. The finding emphasizes the importance of early recognition of bacterial superinfection and sepsis among patients presenting with severe respiratory illness, particularly when clinical deterioration or evidence of systemic infection is present.HRSV-associated disease severity is influenced by age and underlying clinical conditions. Recent multicenter pediatric data have demonstrated increased risk of severe RSV disease among younger children, premature infants, and older children with pulmonary or neurological, neuromuscular, or developmental conditions [24]. In our cohort, children with underlying hematological disorders represented an important high-risk subgroup, and HRSV-associated ARDS was associated with severe clinical outcomes. These findings reinforce the importance of identifying underlying risk factors when assessing patients with HRSV-associated SARI.The ViVI Score provided a structured approach to clinical severity assessment. Previous work has emphasized the importance of standardized severity assessment for respiratory viral illness and SARI [5]. More recent severity scales have also been evaluated to support respiratory hospitalization surveillance and viral genomic surveillance [25]. In our cohort, a ViVI score of ≥30 demonstrated excellent discrimination for mortality, with an AUC of 0.946. This finding supports the potential utility of standardized severity assessment for identifying patients at increased risk of poor outcomes. However, prospective validation in independent populations is required before this threshold can be considered for broader clinical implementation.Raised PCT and CRP concentrations were associated with culture-positive sepsis and adverse clinical outcomes in our cohort. Previous pediatric data have evaluated PCT and CRP as markers of sepsis, with PCT potentially providing useful information regarding bacterial infection and disease severity [26]. However, neither biomarker should be interpreted as a stand-alone diagnostic test. Their value is greatest when interpreted together with the clinical presentation, microbiological findings, and other laboratory parameters.The findings also have implications for respiratory disease surveillance and clinical triage. Integration of rapid molecular diagnostics with standardized severity assessment can provide information on both pathogen circulation and clinical severity [21,22,25]. Such an approach may be particularly valuable in resource-constrained settings, where molecular diagnostic capacity is concentrated at tertiary-care facilities, and timely referral of patients with severe disease remains important. In primary-care settings, recognition of clinical warning signs and timely referral remain essential, while tertiary-care molecular testing can provide additional etiological information.The post-pandemic period is particularly relevant for respiratory pathogen surveillance because changes in population immunity, non-pharmaceutical interventions, and patterns of viral circulation may influence the timing and intensity of respiratory virus activity [16]. Continued surveillance is therefore important for identifying changing epidemiological patterns, detecting populations at increased risk of severe disease, and informing healthcare preparedness.The predominance of HRSV in our cohort also highlights the importance of preventive strategies. Current approaches to prevention of severe RSV disease include maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibody strategies, particularly for infants at greatest risk of severe disease [27]. Continued pathogen-specific surveillance will be important for evaluating the epidemiological impact of these interventions.The study has several strengths. It integrates multiplex molecular diagnostics with conventional microbiological culture, inflammatory biomarkers, and standardized severity assessment, allowing simultaneous evaluation of pathogen distribution, bacterial superinfection, disease severity, and mortality. The use of a standardized severity score also enabled quantitative assessment of the relationship between clinical severity and mortality.In this study, several limitations should nevertheless be considered. The retrospective single-center design and relatively small sample size limit generalizability. The cohort was predominantly pediatric (103 children and 14 adults), which reflects the population evaluated at our center during the study period. Consequently, the findings, particularly those related to pathogen distribution, disease severity, and mortality risk stratification, should be interpreted primarily in the context of pediatric SARI and may not be directly generalizable to adult SARI populations. full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionsHRSV was the predominant respiratory pathogen identified among hospitalized patients with non-SARS-CoV-2 SARI. Multiplex molecular testing provided useful etiological information, while the ViVI Score demonstrated good discriminatory ability for mortality risk in this cohort. Further prospective studies in larger and more diverse populations are needed to validate these findings.
full_text_sections.other: IntroductionSevere acute respiratory infections (SARI) pose a significant global health challenge, causing substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly among vulnerable populations. The World Health Organization (WHO) defines SARI as an acute respiratory illness with a history of fever or measured fever of ≥38°C and cough, with onset within the last 10 days, requiring hospitalization [1]. However, this syndromic definition does not provide information regarding the underlying etiological agent or the individual risk of adverse outcomes. SARI may result from a wide range of viral and bacterial pathogens, and conventional diagnostic methods may not always provide a timely or comprehensive etiological diagnosis.Before the COVID-19 pandemic, SARI detection was largely syndromic, relying on clinical presentation and limited diagnostic capacity [2]. The pandemic acted as a catalyst for strengthening surveillance systems and pathogen identification. In India, surveillance of epidemic-prone diseases is supported through the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme, including laboratory-based and information technology-enabled surveillance [3].SARI constitutes a major cause of healthcare utilization and hospitalization and may require referral to secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities, particularly among young children, older adults, and individuals with underlying comorbidities. Family physicians are often the first point of contact for patients presenting with acute respiratory symptoms and therefore play a pivotal role in early recognition of severe disease, timely referral, initiation of appropriate management, and implementation of infection prevention measures [1,2]. Accurate identification of respiratory pathogens and early risk stratification are essential to improve patient outcomes while minimizing unnecessary antibiotic use [2].In low- and middle-income countries such as India, access to specialized diagnostic services remains limited at primary-care facilities, with sample transport and referral mechanisms used to improve access to diagnostic testing [4]. Consequently, evidence on the etiological profile of SARI and validated clinical severity assessment tools is highly relevant for strengthening referral pathways, antimicrobial stewardship, and respiratory disease surveillance. Such evidence can assist family physicians and primary care providers in identifying patients requiring urgent referral, promoting rational antimicrobial use, and optimizing utilization of healthcare resources [2,4].To standardize clinical assessment, various severity scoring systems have been introduced. One of the most widely recognized is the ViVI Disease Severity Score (ViVI Score), developed by the Vienna Vaccine Safety Initiative. This 22-item composite score quantifies the clinical severity of influenza-like illnesses and SARI across diverse patient populations [5]. It includes indicators of both uncomplicated and complicated disease, providing a standardized framework for clinical decision-making, disease severity assessment, and epidemiological comparison.The advent of multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) platforms has markedly advanced the diagnostic approach to SARI by enabling simultaneous detection of multiple respiratory pathogens from a single clinical specimen, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and expediting clinical decision-making [6]. Integration of rapid molecular diagnostics with standardized severity assessment has the potential to improve clinical risk stratification while strengthening pathogen-specific surveillance and facilitating the integration of virological and clinical data for surveillance and public health applications [6,7].Despite advances in molecular diagnostics and standardized severity assessment, evidence integrating pathogen identification with clinical risk stratification in non-SARS-CoV-2 SARI remains limited, particularly from resource-constrained settings. Addressing this gap may help strengthen clinical decision-making, antimicrobial stewardship, and respiratory infection surveillance across primary and tertiary healthcare settings. papers.title_original: Molecular Etiology and Mortality Risk Stratification of Non-SARS-CoV-2 Severe Acute Respiratory Infection in a Predominantly Pediatric Cohort: A Retrospective Study From a Tertiary Care Hospital in North India

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify the etiological profile of pathogens causing severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) other than SARS-CoV-2 in a pediatric cohort during the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the need to understand non-SARS-CoV-2 causes of SARI in hospitalized children.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care teaching hospital in North India from September to December 2021, focusing on hospitalized patients with SARI who tested negative for SARS-CoV-2. The study population included 103 children and 14 adults, with a male-to-female ratio of 1.81:1.
analysis.methods: Respiratory pathogens were identified using multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) alongside blood and lower respiratory tract cultures. Serum C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and D-dimer levels were measured, and mortality prediction was assessed using the ViVI Score and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.
analysis.main_results: Multiplex PCR detected at least one respiratory pathogen in 69.2% of patients, with human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) A/B being the most frequently identified. No cases of human metapneumovirus were detected, and other pathogens such as Chlamydophila pneumoniae, enterovirus, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were also not found.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the predominance of HRSV in non-SARS-CoV-2 SARI cases among hospitalized children, while also noting the absence of human metapneumovirus detection. This suggests that HRSV may be a more significant pathogen in this context than human metapneumovirus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the etiology of non-SARS-CoV-2 SARI in pediatric populations, which can inform targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias, as it relied on existing clinical data. The evidence for human metapneumovirus absence is based on the lack of detection in the tested cohort, which may not fully represent all possible cases.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational study conducted at a tertiary care hospital in North India from September to December 2021 aimed to determine the etiological profile of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) in hospitalized children, excluding SARS-CoV-2. The study population included 103 children and 14 adults, with a male predominance. Respiratory pathogens were identified using multiplex PCR and cultures, alongside measuring inflammatory markers. Multiplex PCR detected at least one pathogen in 69.2% of patients, with HRSV A/B being the most common. No human metapneumovirus cases were identified, and other pathogens were also absent. The study suggests HRSV may be a more significant cause of SARI in this cohort than human metapneumovirus. The findings have implications for improving surveillance and diagnostics in pediatric populations, particularly in resource-limited settings. However, the study's retrospective nature and potential selection bias limit its generalizability and confidence in the absence of human metapneumovirus detection.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性观察性研究于2021年9月至12月期间在北印度一家三级教学医院进行,聚焦于SARS-CoV-2检测阴性的SARI住院患者。研究人群包括103名儿童和14名成人,男女比例为1.81:1。
elements_zh.methods: 通过多重聚合酶链反应(PCR)结合血液和下呼吸道培养来识别呼吸道病原体。测量了血清C反应蛋白(CRP)、降钙素原(PCT)和D-二聚体水平,并使用ViVI评分和受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线分析评估死亡率预测。
elements_zh.main_results: 多重PCR检测到至少一种呼吸道病原体的患者占69.2%,其中人呼吸道合胞病毒(HRSV)A/B是最常见的病原体。未检测到人偏肺病毒病例,其他病原体如沙眼衣原体肺炎、肠道病毒和肺炎支原体也未被发现。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究突显了HRSV在非SARS-CoV-2 SARI住院儿童中的主导地位,同时指出未检测到人偏肺病毒。这表明HRSV可能比人偏肺病毒在该背景下更为重要。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为了解非SARS-CoV-2 SARI在儿童群体中的病因提供了见解,有助于在资源有限的环境中制定针对性的监测和诊断策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计,可能存在选择偏倚,因为其依赖于现有的临床数据。对于人偏肺病毒缺失的证据是基于在所测试的队列研究中未检测到该病原体,这可能无法完全代表所有可能的病例。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性观察性研究于2021年9月至12月期间在北印度一家三级教学医院进行,聚焦于SARS-CoV-2检测阴性的SARI住院患者。研究人群包括103名儿童和14名成人,男女比例为1.81:1。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过多重聚合酶链反应(PCR)结合血液和下呼吸道培养来识别呼吸道病原体。测量了血清C反应蛋白(CRP)、降钙素原(PCT)和D-二聚体水平,并使用ViVI评分和受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线分析评估死亡率预测。
analysis_zh.main_results: 多重PCR检测到至少一种呼吸道病原体的患者占69.2%,其中人呼吸道合胞病毒(HRSV)A/B是最常见的病原体。未检测到人偏肺病毒病例,其他病原体如沙眼衣原体肺炎、肠道病毒和肺炎支原体也未被发现。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究突显了HRSV在非SARS-CoV-2 SARI住院儿童中的主导地位,同时指出未检测到人偏肺病毒。这表明HRSV可能比人偏肺病毒在该背景下更为重要。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为了解非SARS-CoV-2 SARI在儿童群体中的病因提供了见解,有助于在资源有限的环境中制定针对性的监测和诊断策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计,可能存在选择偏倚,因为其依赖于现有的临床数据。对于人偏肺病毒缺失的证据是基于在所测试的队列研究中未检测到该病原体,这可能无法完全代表所有可能的病例。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of Nirsevimab on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) incidence and to assess the role of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in severe bronchiolitis among young Italian children. The authors highlighted the need to understand hMPV's contribution to disease burden, as it remains under-addressed despite the decline in RSV cases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed data from two seasons of Nirsevimab use in Italy, focusing on young children hospitalized with severe bronchiolitis. It compared the incidence of RSV and hMPV infections during these periods, with a specific emphasis on hMPV as a potential cause of severe disease.
analysis.methods: The authors conducted a retrospective analysis of clinical and virological data from hospitalized children, using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing to identify hMPV and RSV infections. They evaluated the temporal trends in infection rates and compared the clinical outcomes associated with each virus.
analysis.main_results: After two seasons of Nirsevimab use, the decline in RSV cases continued, while hMPV remained a significant cause of severe bronchiolitis. Specifically, hMPV was detected in 15% of hospitalized children, with no substantial reduction in its incidence compared to RSV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that hMPV continues to play a critical role in severe respiratory infections among young children, despite the success of Nirsevimab in reducing RSV cases. This highlights a novel gap in the management of bronchiolitis caused by hMPV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that hMPV should be considered a key pathogen in the surveillance and management of severe respiratory infections in young children, particularly in regions where RSV control measures have been effective.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on existing clinical data, which may introduce bias. However, the evidence is strong given the consistent detection of hMPV in hospitalized children and the observed lack of decline in its incidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of Nirsevimab on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and the continued role of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in severe bronchiolitis among young Italian children. After two seasons of Nirsevimab use, RSV incidence continued to decline, while hMPV remained a significant cause of severe disease. The authors highlight the need for targeted interventions against hMPV, as it has not been adequately addressed by current prevention strategies. The study's findings suggest that hMPV should be prioritized in public health efforts to manage respiratory infections in children. The evidence is based on retrospective clinical data and PCR testing, which provides a strong foundation for the conclusions drawn. However, the study's limitations include potential biases from its observational nature and the lack of direct intervention data on hMPV. The results underscore the importance of addressing hMPV as a distinct pathogen in the context of RSV control.

However, the evidence is strong given the consistent detection of hMPV in hospitalized children and the observed lack of decline in its incidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估Nirsevimab对呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)发病率的影响,并评估人偏肺病毒(hMPV)在意大利婴幼儿严重支气管炎中的作用。作者强调了理解hMPV对疾病负担的贡献的重要性,因为尽管RSV病例有所下降,但hMPV仍未得到充分关注。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了意大利两个Nirsevimab使用季节的数据,重点关注因严重支气管炎住院的婴幼儿。研究比较了这两个时期RSV和hMPV感染的发病率,特别强调hMPV作为严重疾病潜在原因的作用。
elements_zh.methods: 作者对住院儿童的临床和病毒学数据进行了回顾性分析,使用聚合酶链反应(PCR)检测hMPV和RSV感染。他们评估了感染率的时间趋势,并比较了与每种病毒相关的临床结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 在两个Nirsevimab使用季节后,RSV病例的下降趋势持续,而hMPV仍然是严重支气管炎的重要原因。具体而言,hMPV在住院儿童中被检测到的比例为15%,其发病率与RSV相比没有显著减少。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为hMPV在年轻儿童严重呼吸道感染中继续发挥关键作用的证据,尽管Nirsevimab在减少RSV病例方面取得了成功。这突显了在由hMPV引起的支气管炎管理中存在一个新发现的空白。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,hMPV应被视为年轻儿童下呼吸道感染(监测)和严重呼吸道感染管理中的关键病原体,特别是在RSV控制措施已取得成效的地区。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到回顾性设计和依赖现有临床数据的限制,这可能引入偏差。然而,鉴于hMPV在住院儿童中的一致检测以及其发病率未见下降,证据是强有力的。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of Nirsevimab on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) incidence and to assess the role of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in severe bronchiolitis among young Italian children. The authors highlighted the need to understand hMPV's contribution to disease burden, as it remains under-addressed despite the decline in RSV cases.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed data from two seasons of Nirsevimab use in Italy, focusing on young children hospitalized with severe bronchiolitis. It compared the incidence of RSV and hMPV infections during these periods, with a specific emphasis on hMPV as a potential cause of severe disease.
analysis_en.methods: The authors conducted a retrospective analysis of clinical and virological data from hospitalized children, using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing to identify hMPV and RSV infections. They evaluated the temporal trends in infection rates and compared the clinical outcomes associated with each virus.
analysis_en.main_results: After two seasons of Nirsevimab use, the decline in RSV cases continued, while hMPV remained a significant cause of severe bronchiolitis. Specifically, hMPV was detected in 15% of hospitalized children, with no substantial reduction in its incidence compared to RSV.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that hMPV continues to play a critical role in severe respiratory infections among young children, despite the success of Nirsevimab in reducing RSV cases. This highlights a novel gap in the management of bronchiolitis caused by hMPV.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that hMPV should be considered a key pathogen in the surveillance and management of severe respiratory infections in young children, particularly in regions where RSV control measures have been effective.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on existing clinical data, which may introduce bias. However, the evidence is strong given the consistent detection of hMPV in hospitalized children and the observed lack of decline in its incidence.

papers.title: Interactions between respiratory viruses in US adults and children: a prospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Background: The relationship between recent viral infection and subsequent susceptibility to, or protection against, other viruses remains unclear, particularly across ages and symptom status. Methods: A prospective cohort study enrolled participants aged 6 months to 49 years in Washington and Oregon, USA, 2022-2024. Weekly nasal swabs were tested for SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and influenza A/B; additional swabs were collected during symptomatic illness and were also tested for parainfluenza (PIV) 1-4, endemic human coronaviruses (hCOV), adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, human rhinovirus (hRV), and enteroviruses. Proportional hazards regression models were used to characterize associations between incident symptomatic infection (illness) and history of recent illness due to other viruses (within 1-7, 8-14, 15-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180 days), adjusted for geographic region, age, sex, daycare/school/work attendance, household size, and number of children in the household. For SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV, these analyses were repeated to study incidence of infection (including asymptomatic cases). Findings: Of 3,560 participants, 2,969 (83%) had [≥]1 illness over 4,299 person-years. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the interactions between respiratory viruses in US adults and children, focusing on human metapneumovirus. A prospective cohort study enrolled participants aged 6 months to 49 years in Washington and Oregon from 2022 to 2024, collecting weekly nasal swabs for multiple viruses. The study found that recent viral illness was often associated with lower risk of subsequent illness with other viruses, with specific associations noted for human metapneumovirus. The results suggest that viral illnesses may alter short-term susceptibility to other respiratory viruses, with implications for understanding age-specific interactions. However, the study's findings are limited by the observational design and the potential attenuation of associations when including asymptomatic infections.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:近期病毒感染与随后对其他病毒的易感性或保护性之间的关系尚不明确,尤其是在不同年龄和症状状态之间。方法:一项前瞻性队列研究研究于2022年至2024年在美国华盛顿州和俄勒冈州招募了6个月至49岁的参与者。每周采集鼻咽拭子检测SARS-CoV-2、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和流感A/B型病毒;在出现症状时额外采集拭子,并检测副流感病毒(PIV)1-4型、地方性人类冠状病毒(hCOV)、腺病毒、人偏肺病毒、人类鼻病毒(hRV)和肠道病毒。使用比例风险回归模型分析近期病毒感染(疾病)与过去1-7天、8-14天、15-30天、31-60天、61-90天、91-180天内其他病毒感染史之间的关联,调整了地理区域、年龄、性别、托儿所/学校/工作参与情况、家庭规模和家庭中儿童数量。对于SARS-CoV-2、流感和RSV,这些分析重复进行以研究感染的发病率(包括无症状病例)。结果:在3,560名参与者中,2,969名(83%)在4,299人年期间至少发生一次疾病。在疾病发生后短期内(≤2周),调整后的风险比(aHRs)大多低于1,表明近期病毒感染通常与随后其他病毒感染的风险降低相关。在不同年龄组中,近期hRV感染与hCOV、PIV和RSV感染风险降低相关(aHRs 0.07-0.27)。SARS-CoV-2感染则与腺病毒和PIV感染的短期风险增加相关(aHRs 3.20-3.33)。在6个月至4岁的儿童中,近期流感感染与SARS-CoV-2感染的短期风险增加相关。包括无症状感染通常会减弱这些关联。解释:某些病毒感染可能改变随后病毒感染的短期易感性。这些相互作用可能因年龄和症状状态而异。资助:美国疾病控制与预防中心;华盛顿州卫生部。

papers.title: Prospective Cardiac MRI study comparing Recovered COVID-19 patients with Recovered Non-COVID-19 Viral Respiratory Infection Patients (R-COVID-CMR).
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with subclinical myocardial inflammation. Post-COVID-19 infection, there are concerns about subsequent heart failure and persistent myocarditis. It is unknown how COVID-19 infection compares with non-COVID-19 viral infections in terms of myocardial inflammation based on cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) assessment. This prospective longitudinal study aims to determine and compare the extent and severity of myocardial involvement in patients with COVID-19 infection versus non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infections (control). METHOD: Recruited recovered COVID-19 (RCOVID) patients and recovered non-COVID (non-COVID) patients from several hospitals and COVID-19-designated clinic underwent three CMR examinations for functional assessment, native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) quantification, with corroborating blood markers (NT-proBNP, white cell count, c-reactive protein, lactate dehydrogenase, and high sensitivity cardiac troponin T). CMR scans took place (i) within 2-week of confirmed recovery, (ii) 3-month, and (iii) 12-month post-recovery. Linear mixed model with Bonferroni correction was used for analysis. RESULTS: 152 participants were recruited, 112 RCOVID outpatients (mean age: 41.0; 58.9% female) and 40 non-COVID inpatients (mean age:45.0; 37.5% female). Non-COVID infections included influenza virus, rhinovirus/enterovirus, parainfluenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and human metapneumovirus. At all three time points, blood results and cardiac function parameters were not significantly different between RCOVID and non-COVID patient groups (p-value not significant). Both patient groups had no significant differences for native T1/T2 values, ECV, late gadolinium enhancement, T2 short tau inversion recovery, and overall fulfilment of the 2018 revised Lake Louise Criteria at each time points. CONCLUSION: In this prospective longitudinal study with CMR examinations, COVID-19 infection does not cause a worse myocardial inflammatory response than non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infection in terms of CMR parameters, and blood markers. analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to compare the extent and severity of myocardial inflammation in recovered COVID-19 patients with those in recovered non-COVID-19 viral respiratory infection patients using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and blood markers. The study recruited 152 participants, including 112 recovered COVID-19 outpatients and 40 recovered non-COVID-19 inpatients, and conducted three CMR assessments at 2 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months post-recovery. Results showed no significant differences in blood results, cardiac function parameters, or CMR metrics between the two groups at all time points. papers.abstract_zh: 目的:冠状病毒疾病2019(COVID-19)与亚临床心肌炎症有关。在COVID-19感染后,人们担心随后会发生心力衰竭和持续性心肌炎。目前尚不清楚基于心血管磁共振(CMR)评估,COVID-19感染与非COVID-19病毒感染在心肌炎症方面的程度和严重性有何不同。本前瞻性纵向研究旨在比较患有COVID-19感染与非COVID-19病毒呼吸道感染(对照组)的患者的心肌受累程度和严重性。方法:从多家医院和指定的COVID-19诊所招募了恢复期的COVID-19(RCOVID)患者和恢复期的非COVID-19患者,进行了三次CMR检查以评估功能,包括原生T1、T2和细胞外容积(ECV)定量,并结合血液标志物(NT-proBNP、白细胞计数、C反应蛋白、乳酸脱氢酶和高灵敏度心肌肌钙蛋白T)进行验证。CMR扫描分别在确诊恢复后2周内、恢复后3个月和恢复后12个月进行。采用线性混合模型并进行Bonferroni校正进行分析。结果:共招募了152名参与者,其中112名RCOVID门诊患者(平均年龄:41.0岁;58.9%女性)和40名非COVID-19住院患者(平均年龄:45.0岁;37.5%女性)。非COVID-19感染包括流感病毒、鼻病毒/肠病毒、副流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒和人偏肺病毒。在所有三个时间点,RCOVID组和非COVID-19组患者的血液检测结果和心脏功能参数均无显著差异(p值不显著)。两组患者在原生T1/T2值、ECV、晚期钆增强、T2短时反转恢复以及每时间点2018年修订版Lake Louise标准(LLC)的整体符合情况上均无显著差异。结论:在本前瞻性纵向研究中,通过CMR检查发现,与非COVID-19病毒呼吸道感染相比,COVID-19感染在CMR参数和血液标志物方面并未导致更严重的心肌炎症反应。这令人安心,因为先前感染过COVID-19的患者很可能不会发展为心肌炎症或心力衰竭。通俗英语摘要:在冠状病毒疾病2019(COVID-19)暴发期间,一些COVID-19患者偶然被发现存在心脏肌肉层的炎症。医疗专业人员担心这种炎症长期可能导致心脏无法为身体提供足够的血液(即心力衰竭)。因此,我们设计了这项研究,通过将这些患者与其他类型的病毒性呼吸道感染患者(如流感)进行比较,以更好地了解COVID-19患者心脏受累的程度和严重性。我们招募了两组患者,一组是恢复期的COVID-19患者,另一组是恢复期的其他类型病毒性呼吸道感染患者。对每位患者,在其恢复后分别在2周、3个月和12个月时安排三次评估。每次评估时都会采集血液样本,并进行心血管磁共振(CMR)扫描,这是一种用于评估心脏功能的医学影像技术。2018年修订版Lake Louise标准(LLC)是由一组专家推荐的心肌炎症诊断标准。我们根据LLC标准以及血液标志物和心脏功能,对两组患者在每个时间点进行了比较。在我们的研究中,发现COVID-19感染并不比其他类型的病毒性呼吸道感染导致更严重的心肌炎症反应。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 2019冠状病毒病(COVID-19)与亚临床心肌炎有关,在COVID-19感染后,对随后发生心力衰竭和持续性心肌炎存在担忧。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项前瞻性纵向研究旨在确定并比较COVID-19感染患者与非COVID-19病毒性呼吸道感染患者(对照组)的心肌受累程度和严重程度。我们招募了两组患者,一组为从COVID-19感染中康复的患者,另一组为从其他类型的病毒性呼吸道感染中康复的患者。
analysis_zh.main_results: 共招募了152名参与者,其中112名是康复的新冠门诊患者(平均年龄:41.0;女性占比58.9%),40名是非新冠住院患者(平均年龄:45.0;女性占比37.5%)。在所有三个时间点,康复新冠组和非新冠组的血液检测结果和心脏功能参数均无显著差异(p值不显著)。两个患者组在原生T1/T2值、ECV、晚期钆增强、T2短时反转恢复以及每个时间点的2018年修订版Lake Louise标准(LLC)总体符合情况上均无显著差异。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这项前瞻性纵向研究中,通过心脏磁共振成像检查发现,COVID-19感染在心脏磁共振参数和血液标志物方面,并不比非COVID-19病毒性呼吸道感染引起更严重的心肌炎症反应。我们发现,COVID-19感染并不比其他类型的病毒性呼吸道感染引起更严重的心肌炎症反应。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 采用线性混合模型并进行Bonferroni校正进行分析。提供的证据未报告研究结果的普遍适用性。
